To find the minimum strictly positive fractional revival time $t^*$ on the unitary Cayley graph $X = \text{Cay}(\mathbb{Z}_{2p}, \mathbb{Z}_{2p}^\times)$ with $p$ an odd prime, we analyze the transition amplitudes of the continuous-time quantum walk given by $U(t) = e^{-iAt}$.

The eigenvalues of the adjacency matrix $A$ of the unitary Cayley graph are given by the Ramanujan sums $\lambda_j = c_{2p}(j)$:
- For $j = 0$: $\lambda_0 = \phi(2p) = p - 1$
- For $j = p$: $\lambda_p = -(p - 1)$
- For odd $j \neq p$ ($\gcd(j, 2p) = 1$): $\lambda_j = 1$
- For even $j \neq 0$ ($\gcd(j, 2p) = 2$): $\lambda_j = -1$

Using the Fourier basis eigenvectors of the circulant graph, the transition amplitude from vertex $0$ to any vertex $v$ is:
$$U(t)_{v, 0} = \frac{1}{2p} \sum_{j=0}^{2p-1} e^{-i \lambda_j t} e^{-i \pi j v / p}$$

Evaluating this sum for $v \notin \{0, p\}$ yields:
$$2p \cdot U(t)_{v, 0} = \left(e^{-i(p-1)t} - e^{it}\right) + (-1)^v \left(e^{i(p-1)t} - e^{-it}\right)$$

For fractional revival between the antipodal vertices $0$ and $p$, we require $U(t)_{v, 0} = 0$ for all $v \notin \{0, p\}$. Since $p \ge 3$ is an odd prime, there exist both even and odd vertices in $\mathbb{Z}_{2p} \setminus \{0, p\}$. Thus, the coefficients for both $(-1)^v = 1$ and $(-1)^v = -1$ must vanish simultaneously:
$$e^{-i(p-1)t} - e^{it} = 0 \iff e^{ipt} = 1$$

This implies $pt = 2\pi k$ for $k \in \mathbb{Z}^+$. When $pt \in 2\pi\mathbb{Z}$, the amplitudes at vertices $0$ and $p$ become:
$$U(t)_{0, 0} = \cos(t), \quad U(t)_{p, 0} = i\sin(t)$$
which satisfies $|U(t)_{0, 0}|^2 + |U(t)_{p, 0}|^2 = 1$. Since $p$ is an odd prime, $\sin(2\pi/p) \neq 0$ and $\cos(2\pi/p) \neq 0$, ensuring non-trivial fractional revival occurs at the smallest positive integer $k = 1$.

Thus, the minimum strictly positive fractional revival time is $t^* = \frac{2\pi}{p}$.

ANSWER: \frac{2\pi}{p}
